title: Does the .sufr header record the integer width?
body:
A `.sufr` file (format version 6, layout in `libsufr/src/format.rs`) does not record the width of its integers. The header holds `text_len`, and the width follows from it by rule: 4 bytes when `text_len` is under `u32::MAX`, 8 otherwise. `Header::read(filename, int_size)` is told the width by its caller, and `SuffixArray::open_with` picks it from `read_text_length`. The rule is Ken's, from the first writer in c23f773 (2024-10-04), and `origin/dev` applies it the same way at `suffix_array.rs:343`.

The consequence is that a small text written at u64, which `SuffixArrayBuilder::with_force_64bit` does for the tests, is a file the format cannot describe: `open_with` reads it as u32. That hook is sufr-11e453's subject.

## Options

| option | cost |
|---|---|
| keep the rule | nothing changes; a u64 file of a small text stays unreadable through the public API; the u64 path is covered by the unit test at `lib.rs:270` and by real texts over 4 GiB |
| record the width | one header byte, format version 7; every fixture in `data/expected` is rewritten; `open_with` dispatches on the byte; the forced hook can go public and the oracle (`libsufr/tests/oracle.rs`) runs every row at both widths |

Jack chose on 2026-11-03 to keep the rule for now and decide this when the format next changes for its own reasons.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/707e7014
notes.text: A file built with with_force_64bit for a text shorter than u32::MAX cannot be opened through SuffixArray::open_with: it picks the width from text_len and reads the header at 4 bytes, so the sequence starts and the mask come back as garbage. Seen on 2026-11-04 when a test opened such a file. Only TypedSuffixArray::<u64, _, _>::open reads it. The width in the header, or a header read that detects it, is what fixes this.
